notes: Flight Path is a client-only Three.js/Vite app with no backend, accounts, API keys or external services. The only outside reference is a plain GitHub link in the UI; the Earth texture (world.topo.jpg) and plane SVGs are bundled locally. Built with Node 22.12.0, pinned in mise.toml, using `npm ci` and `npx vite build --base=/ --outDir .ui-capture/out` (see .ui-capture/build.sh). The --base=/ flag overrides the repo's GitHub Pages base of '/flight-path/' so the build works from the root of a static server. No source files were changed. Data: the app ships its own real-world dataset in src/common/Data.ts, 34,298 departure/arrival airport coordinate pairs compiled into the bundle. By default it renders 5,000 of them as animated, GPU-instanced planes on dashed great-circle arcs, colored by region. The app keeps no state (no localStorage or URL params), so there is no user data to seed. Main areas: a full-screen 3D globe with a photorealistic Earth texture, atmosphere, day/night shading driven by the real UTC sun position, a starfield and orbit camera controls; an FPS stats panel; and a dat.GUI control panel, collapsed by default per a recent commit, with folders for Flight Controls (flight count 1-30,000, return flights), Flight Path (dash length/gap, hide path), Plane Controls (size, color, speed, elevation, SVG/shape style, hide), Earth Controls (day/night, atmosphere, real-time sun, UTC time slider) and Brightness. A WebGL-capable browser is required. The 18 MB texture loads before the scene appears.
